\chapter{Installation}

\section{Prerequisites}
The agent runs on any Linux host with a systemd-based service manager
and outbound HTTPS access to the collection endpoint. A dedicated
service account is recommended; the package post-install script
creates the account and the state directory if they do not exist.
Disk usage is modest: the binary is 18~MB and the default local
buffer grows to at most 512~MB before oldest batches are dropped.

\section{Package Install}
On Debian-derived hosts install the downloaded package with the
system package manager and then enable the unit. The installer does
not start the service automatically because a valid enrolment token
must be present first. The token file is provisioned by the
configuration management tooling and must be readable only by the
service account.

\section{Configuration}
The unit file passes the listen address through an environment
variable. The service reads its listen address from\footnote{\verb|bind_host| in the unit file, default \verb|127.0.0.1:9464|.}
the environment at startup, and a mismatch with the firewall rule is
the most common cause of a silent install. After editing the unit
file, reload the manager configuration and restart the service.

\section{Verification}
A successful install answers on its diagnostics port within five
seconds of startup. Check the journal for the enrolment line, then
confirm that the first batch was accepted by the collector. If the
journal shows repeated backoff messages, the enrolment token is
expired or the outbound proxy is intercepting the connection.

\chapter{Daily Operation}

\section{Dashboards}
The fleet overview dashboard aggregates the heartbeat stream and
marks any host silent for more than two collection intervals. The
per-host drill-down shows queue depth, batch latency, and the last
hundred diagnostic lines as shipped by the agent.

\section{Upgrades}
Upgrades follow the monthly train. The package manager replaces the
binary in place and restarts the unit; the local buffer survives
restarts, so no batches are lost during a normal upgrade. Hosts that
miss two consecutive trains are flagged on the fleet overview and
should be updated by hand during the next maintenance window.

\section{Troubleshooting}
If a host stops reporting, first check that the service is enabled
and running, then check the diagnostics port locally. A full local
buffer with an idle network usually means the collector endpoint is
rejecting batches; the agent logs the rejection reason once per
minute. Contact the on-call rotation with the host name and the last
rejection line if the cause is not obvious.

\section{Decommissioning}
Before a host is retired, disable the unit, remove the package, and
delete the state directory. The enrolment token must be revoked in
the directory service so that the host identity cannot be reused by
a replacement machine with a recycled name.
